phase: Hays County Poaceae source-key differential verification

records.name: Stapfochloa canterae
records.proposed_life_form: introduced perennial; ecology separate from ID

source_key.character_1: Number of spikelets along 1 cm of raceme
source_key.source: Cerros-Tlatilpa and colleagues, 2015, El género Chloris en México, identification key under old genus Chloris

actual_pixel_review.photo_235666609: True millimeter/centimeter ruler next to several flowering branches. A roughly centered stretch seems relatively open with about 6–10 visually distinguishable spikelets over 1 cm; this is an approximate visual count and not a calibrated mechanical count. Perspective, curvature and overlapping florets produce uncertainty.
actual_pixel_review.photo_235666602: Several distinct mature florets and projecting sterile/other awns lie against millimeter tick marks. Approximate awn length seems a few millimeters; precise attachment and sterile lemma identity cannot be assigned without dissection.
actual_pixel_review.macro_evidence_grade: STRONGER_THAN_HABIT: supports Chloris canterae key over ciliata on apparent branch density; not decisive for all characters

records.next_decisive_action: Count spikelets along 2–3 flat 1-cm rachis segments under a ruler and isolate the upper sterile lemma to measure its exact awn; compare verified S. ciliata at same scale.

records.name: Paspalum langei

source_key.lower_glume: 0.4–1.2(1.8) mm lower glume present; upper glume and lower lemma with papillose-based short pubescence; 2.1–3.3 mm spikelets
source_key.lookalike_hairs: glabrous or sparsely pubescent, hairs typically below 0.1 mm

records.actual_source_review: Three original Hays TEX sheets and labels actually inspected; two November 2021 natural-habitat collections include multiple plants and one explicitly records co-occurring P. pubiflorum. Full sheet scans and field photos lack microscope-level lower glume and papilla-hair demonstration.
records.next_decisive_action: Isolate lower glumes and upper glume/lower lemma pubescence on TEX00568501 or a fresh verified same-specimen Hays collection; compare matched P. pubiflorum spikelet under 10–20×.
records.source_note: 2023 Hawaii treatment calls P. langei annual although GrassBase and FNA describe it as perennial. For local ID do NOT use annual-vs-perennial as the decisive character without resolving publication inconsistency.

records.name: Tridentopsis elongata

taxon_concepts.Flora_of_North_America: FNA account under Tridentopsis mutica includes both varieties/concepts
taxon_concepts.local_1999_Flora: Tridens muticus var. elongatus regional older combination

diagnostic.elongata: upper glumes generally around 5.5–10 mm, with 3–7 veins (variety-level key)
diagnostic.mutica: upper glumes usually 4–6 mm, mostly single-veined; overlap in length
diagnostic.requirement: Direct glume vein count on one isolated glume with mm scale, paired with verified current mutica.

records.photos_checked: Four high-resolution iNaturalist Hays photos show overlapping glumes, mature heads, and foliage, but none isolates an upper glume so nervation count is unambiguous.
records.record_false_positive_warning: Two earlier Hays TEX specimens with Tridens muticus var. muticus are verified different-name taxa and must not be counted as elongata vouchers.
records.next_decisive_action: Photo/dissection of complete second glume including base, upper half and 1-mm scale, count nerves under backlighting; cross-check flora source concept.

policy: Regional Flora is key for Central Texas morphological characters; recent Kew taxon concepts may differ. This review identifies additional characters actually inspectable in source photos, without overwriting live 112 species.
